response:
Diagnosis from generation 6: the consolidated specification worked — LongMemoryDepreciationShortfallVsDebtCoverage is now the archive leader on every dimension simultaneously (FMB −4.36, alpha −4.3%, t = −4.41, Sharpe −0.52), confirming that the five-year own-norm benchmark and the interest-bearing-debt denominator are complementary, not competing, improvements. Three further lessons: (i) the maturity wall works as a *standalone* distress leg (FMB −3.32, alpha −3.5%, t = −3.52, Sharpe −0.39) with no coverage or profitability information in it, so refinancing timing is a genuine second conditioning dimension; (ii) adding net-debt stock produced the archive's biggest alpha (−5.3%, t = −4.74) but again halved the slope, so skewed stock ratios help tails and hurt slopes; (iii) the level control confirmed the mechanism is within-firm policy drift, since the level version kept a slope but lost most of the alpha (−2.0%, t = −1.94). This round blends the two validated debt channels, pushes the memory horizon one step further, tests two scale-free reconstructions of the shortfall, and opens one new distress dimension (operating contraction).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ShortfallVsCoverageAndMaturityWall
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc))), RATIO(dlc, ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is truly refinancing-constrained when it both lacks cash earnings to service its debt and must roll a large share of that debt imminently, and it is exactly these firms whose sustained depreciation shortfall represents covenant-motivated earnings management.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Coverage and maturity share are the two distress legs that each worked independently, they measure serviceability versus timing so their errors should be largely uncorrelated, and both are bounded, smoothly distributed ratios — unlike the net-debt stock blend that sacrificed the FMB slope. This is the most promising consolidation available and should improve both forms of evidence rather than trading them off.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: SevenYearNormShortfallVsDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 7)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Because depreciation policy drifts over the multi-year life of an asset base, a seven-year norm should capture even more accumulated deferred expense than a five-year norm, provided enough firms have the required history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Extending the window from one year to three to five monotonically improved the slope (−2.98, −3.73, −4.36) with no coverage loss, so the horizon has not yet been shown to saturate and one more step is the cheapest remaining test of the mechanism's timescale. Coverage relative to 0.124 is the decisive diagnostic: if it falls materially the gain would be a survivorship artifact and the five-year specification should stand.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ProportionalDepreciationShortfallVsDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5), RATIO(dp, at)), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A 0.5 percentage-point drop in the depreciation rate is trivial for a capital-intensive utility charging 10% of assets but represents a quarter of the expense for an asset-light firm charging 2%, so the economically comparable measure of stretching is the *proportional* shortfall relative to the firm's own normal rate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The absolute deviation mechanically loads the short leg with heavy-asset industries, which is likely why industry-neutralizing the accrual leg was roughly break-even — the sector tilt is a scaling artifact rather than information. Normalizing by the firm's own norm removes the capital-intensity scale without discarding cross-industry information, and should raise the slope and Sharpe together.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: OrdinalDepreciationPositionVsDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
HYPOTHESIS: What identifies a manipulator is that its current depreciation rate sits at the bottom of its own recent history, regardless of the size of the gap, since the ordinal position is immune to one-off asset sales, acquisitions, and restatements that distort the magnitude.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The five-year peak benchmark underperformed the mean benchmark on the slope (−2.77 versus −4.36), suggesting extreme-value anchors are noisy; an ordinal position statistic uses the entire history yet remains robust to those same outliers. Comparing it against the mean-deviation leader tells us whether the signal lives in the magnitude of the shortfall or merely in its ordering.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: ShortfallUnderCoverageAndRevenueContraction
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc))), NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Shrinking revenue is the clearest evidence that an asset base has become economically impaired, so a firm that is simultaneously contracting, weakly covered, and charging less depreciation than its own norm is deferring an impairment that the market has not yet priced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every distress leg tested so far is financial; operating contraction is a real-side fragility dimension that is a standard bankruptcy predictor and is only weakly correlated with coverage ratios. It also directly addresses the economic premise of the depreciation channel — assets should be written down faster, not slower, when the business they serve is shrinking.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: TripleProductShortfallCoverageMaturity
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc))))), RANK(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dltt, dlc))))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing is concentrated in the joint tail where all three conditions hold at once — sustained depreciation suppression, weak debt-service capacity, and an imminent maturity wall — so a conjunctive score should isolate a smaller but far more extreme short leg.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Signal 1 aggregates the two distress channels additively, which lets a firm score highly on distress through one channel alone, whereas the triple product requires both, so the pair jointly identifies whether the interaction is conjunctive or compensatory. If the triple product delivers a larger alpha with a similar t-stat, the tails are where the economics lives and the final generation should concentrate there.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
